title: Flight results show the wrong route
scenario: You are on the MakeMyTrip flight search team. A tester reported that search results sometimes do not match the route they last searched for.
symptom: Searching Delhi → Mumbai and then quickly searching Bengaluru → Hyderabad, before the first search responds, ends with the page correctly showing a "Bengaluru → Hyderabad" heading, but the flight cards listed underneath are still Delhi → Mumbai's — the slower first search's response arrives later and overwrites the newer results.
hints: Try a slow route first (Delhi → Mumbai), then immediately search a fast one (Bengaluru → Hyderabad) before the first finishes. Watch what the results show once both responses have arrived.
search() in useFlightSearch.js calls setResults as soon as its own response arrives, with no way to tell whether a newer search has started since.
Give each call to search() a way to know if it's still the most recent one — for example a counter or ref that only the latest call's response is allowed to act on.

rubric.description: search() tags or tracks each outgoing request (e.g. a request id or ref) so that, when a response arrives, it can tell whether that response belongs to the most recently started search before using it.

Searching Delhi→Mumbai and then immediately searching Bengaluru→Hyderabad, before the first response arrives, ends with Bengaluru→Hyderabad's flights shown — even once the slower Delhi→Mumbai response arrives afterward.

The fix does not work by disabling, debouncing, or otherwise preventing a new search from starting until the previous one resolves. A second search can still be started immediately after the first, and it is still that second search's response that ends up displayed.
A single search with no overlapping requests still updates the results and clears the loading state normally.
